Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment — A thermally strong day with sharp lapse rates (9.1–9.9 °C/km) and domain-wide peak w* 679 ft/min. High cloud cover (73–91%) but no overdevelopment. Several sites have off-wind directions for ridge soaring, while low-level wind shear affects Hallelujah, McClellan, West McClellan, and Duck Hill. Recommended for experienced pilots only due to sharp thermals and shear hazards.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal. Wind direction off for ridge soar (N/NE vs preferred SE), but thermals workable. Best window 10am–3pm: peak w* 307 ft/min, thermal ceiling 3004 ft AGL. Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only.
  • Hallelujah: Marginal. Strong E/SE winds (peak 23 mph) opposite preferred W/SW, limiting ridge lift; thermal soaring possible afternoon as wind eases. Best window 12pm–5pm: peak w* 430 ft/min, ceiling 4534 ft AGL. Low-level speed shear 6 mph/layer. Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only. Evening winds remain off.
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable. Light winds align with preferred S/SE; good thermal development. Best window 9am–3pm: peak w* 338 ft/min, ceiling 2309 ft AGL. Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only.
  • McClellan: Favorable. Very light winds (max 7 mph) and strong thermals, though wind direction slightly off preferred. Best window 10am–5pm: peak w* 464 ft/min, ceiling 6942 ft AGL. Low-level speed shear 6 mph/layer. Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only.
  • West McClellan: Marginal. Wind direction opposite preferred (E vs W), but light speeds allow thermal flying. Best window 11am–5pm: peak w* 445 ft/min, ceiling 6853 ft AGL. Significant low-level shear (5 mph speed, 30° direction). Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only.
  • Peavine Mountain: Favorable. Morning winds within preferred S/SE, good thermals. Best window 9am–4pm: peak w* 373 ft/min, ceiling ~3057 ft AGL. Wind becomes cross after 1pm. Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable. Wind aligns with preferred NE/E most of day, strong thermals. Best window 9am–4pm: peak w* 463 ft/min, ceiling 4867 ft AGL. Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only.
  • Duck Hill: Favorable. Morning wind off, but shifts to preferred NW/N after 1pm; strong thermals and excellent evening ridge potential. Best window 1pm–6pm (thermal) and evening ridge soar after 6pm with W-NW-N winds 5–10 mph. Peak w* 459 ft/min, ceiling 7681 ft AGL. Low-level shear (6 mph speed, 30° direction). Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable. Very weak thermals (peak w* 126 ft/min) and generally off-wind. Brief, weak ridge window late afternoon (0–2 mph). No reliable flying window. Sharp thermals — advanced pilots only (moot due to weak lift).

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals: Lapse rates 9.1–9.9 °C/km at all sites — suitable only for advanced/expert pilots.
  • Low-level wind shear (hazardous speed shear ≥5 mph/layer or directional shear ≥30°/layer):
    • Hallelujah: 6 mph/layer speed shear at 1,366 ft AGL.
    • McClellan: 6 mph/layer speed shear at 7,242 ft AGL.
    • West McClellan: 5 mph/layer speed shear at 7,859 ft AGL & 30° directional shear.
    • Duck Hill: 6 mph/layer speed shear at 8,754 ft AGL & 30° directional shear.
  • Icing: Potential above freezing level (14,375 ft MSL) if climb-outs reach cloud base (domain LCL up to 19,177 ft MSL).
  • Visibility: High average cloud cover (73–91% at sites) may reduce visibility; check NOTAMs/PIREPs.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
